1.explanation:
• tree-select/index.en-us.md & index.md: Provide the TreeSelect API definitions (checkable, defaultValue, disabledItemCheckbox) and explain intended behavior when default selecting disabled nodes.
• tree-select/adaptor/index.jsx: Contains the core logic for merging defaultValue with checked state, rendering selected tags, and assigning keys — where the duplicate-key bug likely originates.
• tree-select/demo/check.md: Demonstrates multiple-check behavior; a reference for how defaultValue and disabled items should interact under normal circumstances.
• tree/adaptor/index.jsx: Underlying Tree component’s node rendering and key/pos generation logic, which influences TreeSelect’s key assignment for selected items.
• tree-select/theme/index.jsx: Renders the selection tags (spans) in the input; reviewing this shows how tag keys are constructed and where duplicates appear.
1.bug_scenario: In the provided CodePen screenshot, the TreeSelect is initialized with multiple selection (checkable) alongside a defaultValue that references a disabled tree node ("Input"). On initial render, the disabled item is already selected, but its label (“Input”) is rendered multiple times as tags inside the input box (four duplicates in the red-highlighted area). The console also warns about duplicate React keys for these tags. Essentially, default-selecting a disabled node causes duplicate tag rendering and non-unique key generation.
